data.title: Prices fall on milder temperature forecasts, strong Norwegian supply
data.description:
Key points:
  • Milder temperatures expected on latest weather run
  • Supply from Norway rises
  • Europe's gas stores 67.20% full

Dutch and British gas prices fell on Friday morning as forecasts for milder temperatures curbed demand and supply from Norway rose.

The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was down €3.428 at €84.40 per megawatt hour (MWh) or around $27.10 /mmBtu, by 0918 GMT, ICE data showed.

The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) was down 9.47 pence at 208.30 pence per therm.

“Weather across north-west Europe is set to get warmer on the DA (day-ahead)," said LSEG gas analyst Dzmitry Dauhalevich, with the forecast 3 degrees Celsius higher than previously at 3.5C.

Local distribution zone demand, which includes heating demand, is forecast 623 gigawatt hours/day lower at 4,353 GWh/d for the day-ahead, LSEG data showed.

Norwegian exports to continental Europe, which have been curbed by outages and maintenance this week, were forecast to rise by 35 million cubic metres day to 341 mcm/d, LSEG data showed.

In Britain, strong wind power output also led to lower gas demand.

Peak wind power output was forecast at 19.9 gigawatts on Friday and 19.7 GW for Saturday, Elexon data showed.

Europe, however, remains vulnerable to cold weather shocks with gas stores at low levels.

Germany, Europe’s largest gas consumer, “faces the lowest stock levels in more than a decade heading into winter, and the weather forecasts so far look cold for at least the first week of December,” analysts at Mind Energy said.

Europe’s gas stores are currently 67.20 % full, the latest data from Gas Infrastructure Europe showed.

In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract <> was up €0.91 at €85.06 euro a metric ton.

data.title: Arms Maker Rheinmetall Slashes Midterm Forecasts After Order Setbacks
data.description:
(09:03 GMT) *Rheinmetall Cuts 2030 Sales View
(09:04 GMT) *Rheinmetall Sees 2030 Sales Between EUR33B and EUR37B, Prior Roughly EUR50B
(09:05 GMT) *Rheinmetall Raises 2030 Oper Margin View
(09:05 GMT) *Rheinmetall Sees 2030 Oper Margin Of About 20%, Prior About 15.5%
(09:06 GMT) *Rheinmetall Backs 2030 Cash Conversion Rate View
(09:06 GMT) *Rheinmetall Sees 2030 Cash Conversion Rate Above 50%
(09:18 GMT) *Correct: Rheinmetall Cuts 2030 Oper Margin View
(09:19 GMT) *Correct: Rheinmetall Sees 2030 Oper Margin Of About 20%, Prior Above 20%
(09:28 GMT) Arms Maker Rheinmetall Slashes Midterm Forecasts After Order Setbacks

By Mauro Orru

Rheinmetall lowered its sales and margin projections for the end of the decade, a sign that it doesn't expect to grow as strongly as it previously forecast after the German government canceled a big frigate order and delayed procurement of a lucrative combat-vehicle project.

The German defense group said its 2030 sales should range between 33 billion euros and 37 billion euros, equivalent to between $36.20 billion and $40.58 billion. The company had previously expected 2030 sales of about 50 billion euros.

Meanwhile, its closely watched operating margin should come in at about 20% at the end of the decade compared with a prior forecast of above 20%. Its cash conversion rate is still expected above 50%.

The revisions show that Rheinmetall is moving to recalibrate expectations for the coming years following a number of setbacks in recent months that weighed on its stock and led some analysts to question whether the midterm targets it had tweaked last year were still achievable. Rheinmetall slashed its 2026 guidance twice this year and its shares are down nearly 50% since early January.

data.title: TVS Motor Company Introduces TVS Armado, a New Cargo Tricycle
data.description:
TVS Motor Company, part of TVS VENU, and a reputed global manufacturer of two and three-wheelers, today announced the global launch of TVS Armado – the best-in-class cargo tricycle with 1 ton load capacity. With this launch TVS expands its commercial mobility portfolio with a tricycle designed to address the evolving needs of cargo transportation and first and last-mile logistics.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261126523378/en/

Beyond the product itself, TVS Armado is backed by the assurance associated with the TVS Motor brand. The company's focus on quality, reliability, genuine spare parts availability, trained service personnel and customer support is intended to help commercial users maintain their vehicles and businesses with confidence.

Recognizing the needs of entrepreneurs, fleet owners, delivery businesses - TVS Armado has been developed with a customer-first approach, translating real-world operating requirements into a dependable mobility solution that is designed to keep businesses moving day in, day out.

The TVS Armado is powered by a robust 200 cc oil-cooled engine, delivering 10.6 kW of maximum power at 7,500 rpm and 15.5 Nm of peak torque at 5,000 rpm, paired with a five-speed manual transmission. Designed for demanding commercial mobility solutions, it features a 16-litre fuel tank to support extended operating hours. Its two-metre long cargo bed offers a vast loading area with payload capacity of up to 1 ton, enabling businesses to transport a wide range of goods efficiently. The large cargo bed, along with 230 mm of ground clearance and strong leaf spring suspension is designed to support operations across varied road conditions, including urban, suburban and rural routes. The first in industry oil-cooled engine is designed to offer a practical balance of durability and ease of maintenance, backed with the best-in-category warranty terms which reinforces customer confidence in long-term ownership.

Speaking at the global launch, Peyman Kargar, President, International Business, TVS Motor Company said, “TVS Motor has always believed in providing innovative mobility solutions. With TVS Armado, we become the first globally reputed OEM to enter the tricycle cargo segment, bringing an innovative, best-in-class product to the 1 ton cargo mobility space. First- and last-mile logistics is critical to businesses and communities, and TVS Armado is designed around the real needs of customers and business owners, combining load-carrying capability, world-class reliability and durability with the practicality required for everyday commercial use.

“As we build our commercial mobility portfolio globally, TVS Armado reflects our ambition to create solutions that deliver tangible business value and contribute to the growth of communities. TVS Armado aims to be a reliable business partner for those who work relentlessly to build a better future, in line with TVS Motor’s vision of transforming the quality of life of people across the world by providing mobility solutions that are exciting, responsible, sustainable and safe.”

With TVS Armado, TVS Motor Company builds on its experience in commercial mobility to address the evolving needs of cargo transportation. TVS Armado aims to be a reliable business partner for those who work relentlessly to build a better future across the regions of Africa, Latin America and ASEAN.

For more information, please visit www.tvsmotor.com

data.title: Bulletin from the extraordinary general meeting in Alligator Bioscience AB
data.description:
Today, on 27 November 2026, an extraordinary general meeting was held in Alligator Bioscience AB. A summary of the adopted resolutions follows below.

Resolution on (A) directed issue of ordinary shares (equalization issue); (B) amendment of the Articles of Association; and (C) reverse split of ordinary shares

The meeting resolved, in accordance with the board of directors' proposal, on a consolidation of ordinary shares (so-called reversed share split) whereby one thousand (1,000) existing ordinary shares are consolidated into one (1) ordinary share (1:1,000). The purpose of the reverse share split is to achieve an appropriate number of shares for the company. In order to enable the reverse share split and to achieve an even quota value after the reverse share split, the meeting also resolved on a directed issue of ordinary shares (equalization issue).

Through the equalization issue, the company's share capital increases by SEK 0.76 through the issue of 152 new ordinary shares at a subscription price of SEK 0.005 per share, corresponding to the share's quota value. With deviation from the shareholders' preferential rights, the new ordinary shares can only be subscribed for by Vator Securities AB. The reason for the deviation from the shareholders' preferential rights and for setting the subscription price at the quota value is that the new issue is being carried out to achieve a total number of ordinary shares in the company that is evenly divisible by the consolidation ratio and thus to achieve an even quota value after the reverse share split.

The reverse share split means that the number of ordinary shares, which after the directed issue (equalization issue) amounts to a total of 3,568,107,000, is reduced to a total of 3,568,107. The reverse share split also means that the quota value of the share increases from SEK 0.005 to SEK 5.

To enable the reverse share split, it was also resolved to amend § 5 of the Articles of Association so that the limits for the number of shares in the company are changed to not less than 3,000,000 and not more than 12,000,000.

The board of directors was authorized to determine the record date for the reverse share split, which may not be earlier than the date on which the resolution on the reverse share split has been registered with the Swedish Companies Registration Office. Further information on the procedure for the reverse share split will be published in connection with the board of directors' decision regarding the record date.

Resolution on authorization for the board of directors to resolve on issues of warrants

The meeting resolved to authorize the board of directors, within the limits set forth in the Articles of Association, up until the next annual general meeting, at one or several occasions, with deviation from the shareholders’ preferential rights, resolve to issue warrants. The right to subscribe for the warrants shall be granted solely to Fenja Capital II A/S (“Fenja Capital”). The warrants shall be issued free of charge.

The purpose of the authorization and the reasons for the deviation from the shareholders' preferential rights and that the warrants are issued free of charge is to fulfil the company's obligations to Fenja Capital under the loan agreement entered into by the company and Fenja Capital in July 2026 (and as further described in the company's press releases from 23 July 2026 and 29 September 2026). According to the loan agreement, Fenja Capital has received warrants series 2026/2031. The warrants are subject to terms and conditions that contain  recalculation terms that entail a so-called “full dilution protection”, meaning that Fenja Capital, with certain exceptions, shall be compensated in the event of certain corporate actions so that Fenja Capital always has the right to be allocated additional warrants so that the warrants held by Fenja Capital together entail the same dilution as the warrants represented immediately prior to the corporate action, calculated on the number of outstanding ordinary shares in the company. According to the loan agreement, Fenja Capital also has the right to request recalculation of already issued warrants series 2026/2031, which may require the issuance of new warrants of the same series to replace the already issued warrants.

Election of board members as well as remuneration for the board members

The meeting resolved in accordance with the proposal from the Nomination Committee that the board shall consist of three ordinary board members elected by the general meeting. The meeting further resolved in accordance with the proposal from the Nomination Committee to re-elect Hans-Peter Ostler and Anna Törner as board members and to elect Søren Bregenholt as new board member. Hans-Peter Ostler was re-elected as Chairman of the board. The previous board members Denise Goode and Jörg Möller were not proposed for re-election. In connection with the meeting, the employee representative Karin Nordbladh resigned from her seat on the board.

In addition to this, the meeting resolved in accordance with the proposal from the Nomination Committee regarding reduced board remuneration, meaning that remuneration to the board shall be paid with SEK 455,000 to the Chairman of the board of directors and with SEK 210,000 to each of the other board members who are not employed by the company. Remuneration for committee work shall be unchanged and be paid with SEK 125,000 to the Chairman of the Audit Committee, with SEK 50,000 to each of the other members of the Audit Committee, with SEK 50,000 to the Chairman of the Remuneration Committee and with SEK 25,000 to each of the other members of the Remuneration Committee. Søren Bregenholt shall not receive board or committee remuneration during the time he remains as CEO of the company, i.e. up to and including 31 December 2026. The reduced fees will apply from and including the extraordinary general meeting until the next annual general meeting, pro rata.

data.title: Volatile STOXX set for best week in six months
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX up 1%, as stock markets bounce globally
  • Miners, tech lead gains
  • S&P futures up 2%

VOLATILE STOXX SET FOR BEST WEEK IN SIX MONTHS

It's been a volatile old week in stock markets.

The STOXX is 1% higher in the first hour or so of trading, and is now up 2.7% on the week, set for its biggest weekly gain in about six months, even despite reasonable falls on both Tuesday and Wednesday.

Mining and tech stocks are doing the heavy lifting, up 4% and 2.6% respectively, as metal prices jump and the chip complex bounces back. (.SXPP), (.SX8P)

The tech moves are part of global dip buying. Chip-heavy Korean and Japanese benchmarks are also higher, and that in turn is feeding into metal prices, as is equities buying from China's national team.

Banks are also catching a lift as traders buy what had been sold. (.SX7P)

There are few idiosyncratic single stock stories out there, or at least they are getting overwhelmed by the bigger picture.

French drugmaker Sanofi dipped 1.6% after gaining close to 18% over the last five sessions on market optimism around its latest acquisition, US drugmaker Insmed.

Commerzbank is underperforming the broader market again, down 2% after Italy's UniCredit on Thursday sought a management shake-up as it cleared all regulatory steps to take control of its rival.

data.title: Stock Futures Jump as AI Trade Set for Rebound
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

U.S. stock futures are poised to open in the green for a shortened trading session Friday, as the artificial-intelligence trade rebounds at the end of a volatile week.

Nasdaq futures trade 2.7% higher, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.8% and 1.15% respectively. Stocks across the AI ecosystem rallied premarket, with Nvidia gaining around 4.5%.

Signs of a rebound follow choppy trade earlier in the week. However, the AI trade isn't out of the woods yet, XTB research director Kathleen Brooks said.

"While technical indicators suggest that a recovery could be on the cards, the fundamental problems surrounding the AI trade remain," Brooks said. "The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered, for example, concerns about the profitability of the AI trade and financing costs."

Gains in the U.S. premarket followed a bullish session in Asia. South Korea's memory chip-dominated Kospi jumped 4.3%, while stock indexes in Shanghai and Hong Kong rose after Chinese authorities reiterated their support for capital markets. European equity indexes rallied at the open, with AI-related stocks leading the charge. The continent's Stoxx 600 index rose 0.95% in early trade.

Improved sentiment in equity markets bled into metals, too. Silver contracts jumped more than 10% to $44.11 a troy ounce, while gold futures added close to 4% to trade around $3,680 an ounce.

Oil prices continued to rise, with benchmark Brent crude contracts gaining 1% to trade around $97.50 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts jumped 2.6% to trade around $85.90 a barrel.

Treasurys weakened amid investors' shift back to risk and hardened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. Ten-year yields rose more than seven basis points to trade above 4.900%, while two-year yields rose toward 4.700%. The Fed enters a blackout period on Saturday ahead of its December meeting, with expectations for a 25 basis point rise priced in at 99%, according to LSEG.

The dollar edged higher against a basket of global currencies but remained below highs hit earlier this week. Bitcoin was helped by broader ebullient market sentiment, rising 1.5% to trade around $61,670.

Spanish voters head to the polls on Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez looks to stay in power. Next week, Nvidia's reinstated Chief Executive Jensen Huang will appear in front of Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Write to Joe Stonor at josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com
